title: Rebuild the page where Daniel answers questions from the studio: how long each will take him, the questions grouped by topic, and one place to read each
tier_reason: HQ page; git reverts it; shown to Daniel as a result, not asked
ask:
Build the reader in docs/QUEUE_TO_ZERO.md §6–§7 from the mock docs/design/mockups/queue_to_zero/queue_reader.html (build_mock.py shows how the real cards map onto it). Replaces #/work. Left: the band (count, minutes at his pace, picks vs reads), the 'coming back to you' strip, questions grouped by `subject` (a field the chief of staff sets when prepping; ungrouped items under 'Everything else'), each row = one-sentence question, recommended answer, Yes, Talk, a cost chip; folds for 'Landed without you' (with Undo per line) and 'Back with the studio'. Right: the fixed anatomy — question; what I recommend and why and instead; options; what yes starts with each follow-up marked lands-on-its-own or comes-back-as-a-question; what you would be walking back; so far; evidence folded; Yes/No/Talk. Decision cards and work cards render through one anatomy. Keys j/k/y/t; the pane advances after a verdict. Every sentence per docs/WRITING.md. Keep hq/static/work.js's verdict endpoints; the page is presentation.

Layout note from Daniel, 2026-09-21: on the old page the line above the follow-on tasks ('Accepting files exactly this') did not read as a heading over a list, so he read 'files' as a noun. In the reader, 'What yes starts' is an unmistakable heading over the list, and the list items are visibly items.

RE-AIMED 2026-09-21: do NOT edit hq/static/work.js or hq/static/work.css — another session holds them and any patch touching them parks. Build hq/static/queue.js and hq/static/queue.css instead: queue.js registers routes['/work'] and routes['/inbox'] and its <script> tag goes AFTER work.js in hq/static/index.html so its registration wins; add the css link beside work.css. Reuse work.js's endpoints as they are (GET /api/work, POST /api/work/accept, /drop, /approve, /respond with {id, comment}). The Work page is then the reader at the same address; work.js stays untouched.
first_action: Open the mock beside the current #/work, list every field each card type needs for the anatomy, and start from the band and the row, which need no new server data.
source_message: Daniel said yes to the arrival rule (S-16) and the spawn rule (S-17) on 2026-09-20; docs/QUEUE_TO_ZERO.md §12 is the build order.

result:
This finishes what the earlier attempt started. Here's where it stands:

**What changed since the last attempt:** the queue reader now has its side pane (§7 of the design doc). Earlier I'd built the left side only — the cost band, the strip, questions grouped by subject, and the two read-only folds. Clicking a question (or `j`/`k`) now fills the right side with the fixed anatomy: what I recommend and why and instead; the options on a decision card; what saying yes starts, with the follow-up list under an actual "What yes starts" *heading* over an actual list — the exact thing you flagged on the old Work page, where the lead-in sentence let you read "files" as a noun instead of seeing a heading over items; what a "no" would walk back; the conversation so far; and the evidence (the write-up, the diffstat, the suites, the checker's verdict, the original brief) folded and closed by default. Yes/No/Talk sit at the bottom, and a verdict advances the pane to the next question by itself, since the row you just acted on simply drops out of the next reload.

Talk moved out of an inline box under every row and into the pane's own composer, matching your mock — the row's Talk button just opens the pane and focuses it.

Nothing about the endpoints changed. This is still presentation over `work.js`'s existing `/api/work/*` and `/api/ruling` — I didn't touch `work.js` or `work.css`, per your instruction to leave those to the other session.

**What I checked:** the JS parses clean, brace-matched CSS, and I traced every field the pane reads back to real data in `hq/data/work/*.json` and `hq/data/decisions/*.json` — nothing is invented or hard-coded. I did not open it in a browser: HQ is already running on this machine and I was told not to start a second copy, so this is verified by reading and static checks only, not by clicking through it.

**Still open, and already on record in the doc, not new gaps:** subject grouping has no real data yet (every question lands under "Everything else" until prepping writes a `subject` field), and §7a — which of three briefing forms (line / gallery / before-and-after) a question gets — is still yours to rule on.

Committed to this worktree's branch, not yet on `origin/main` — that lands when the chief of staff reads this diff, per the drain process. Safe to archive once that happens; nothing here is uncommitted or at risk of being lost in the meantime.
